newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan preparing law to curb unions, paper says.
newsitem.headline: Jordan preparing law to curb unions, paper says.

text.p: A Jordanian newspaper said on Wednesday the government was preparing a law to curb the power of Jordan's influential, opposition-dominated professional unions.

Al-Arab Al-Yawm daily quoted sources as saying the government would announce a law next week which would prevent professional unions, fierce critics of Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel, from political activities.
It would also restrict the size and influence of the 13 unions, many of them dominated by Islamists, by ending compulsory worker membership, the paper added.
The new law would "concentrate on 'professionalising' the unions and making members discuss only questions of their profession," it said.
Officials could not immediately confirm or deny the report.
Jordan's government has frequently rebuked the unions, most recently for their public opposition to tough amendments to Jordan's press law announced last month.

The amended law, issued during a parliamentary recess just months before scheduled elections, was criticised by the U.S. group Human Rights Watch which said it appeared aimed more at barring critical reporting than protecting national interests.
Four union chiefs resigned in protest at the law.

"The professional associations have not only taken over the role of the political parties and overlooked their basic mission of serving their members' professional interests," Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed was quoted as saying by the Jordan Times on Wednesday. "They have gone beyond that to infringe on the powers of the government, and this is totally unacceptable."
Rasheed added that the constitutional right to form a union in Jordan applied only to labourers, not professionals.
"Democracy is not a free-for-all system," the paper quoted him as saying in an interview, which did not mention plans for a new law.
